name: reachability
description: REACHABILITY ratchet. `tsc`, the test suite and every existing lint gate check TYPES and BEHAVIOUR; nothing checked whether a thing is REACHED. CLAUDE.md names 'built but unwired' as this repo's single most common defect, and every instance (services/lateFees, services/respa/earlyIntervention, calculateFlipAnalysis, taxSaleAuctions/taxSaleListings, achMandateSetup/achAutopayRun, rental_units.kind='pad', routes-contract-chain.ts, the rent-roll importer's unitKind arg) shipped GREEN and was found hours later by a manual audit. This converts that recurring audit into CI. Every count is strictly down-only, and raising one requires explicit founder/Iris-CTO sign-off (see lastBumpNote for the exceptions actually invoked): exports in server/services|jobs with no production call site; pgTables with no writer; pgTables with no reader; routes-*.ts never mounted; exports the gate cannot assert on because their module is dynamically imported in a way that hides which exports are touched; and service/job files nothing imports at all. Family 1 is TWO rules, split 2026-08-20: `unreachedExports` is the accusation (nothing anywhere references the symbol) and `internalOnlyExports` is the narrower complaint (exported, but used only inside its own module — drop the keyword, keep the code). They are baselined apart because merged, the second buried the first four to one. The count of families is deliberately not stated here — it said 'four' for as long as there were four, and would have said it forever. THE CHEAPEST WAY TO SATISFY THIS GATE IS DELETION — the north star is a smaller codebase, and every reduction must be locked in by the commit that earned it (a stale-high baseline FAILS, same as `as-any`).
minimaNote: VACUITY FLOORS, not ratchets. Every baseline above counts BAD THINGS FOUND, so a scan that stops seeing files finds zero and reports six reassuring PASS lines — this repo has already been bitten by exactly that (a block-comment stripper that mispaired and blanked the very lines a scan was counting). These floor the SCAN POPULATIONS the run prints, and the gate exits nonzero if any drops below or is missing entirely. Seeded 2026-08-16 at roughly 75-80% of live (productionFiles 2520, exportFiles 917, pgTables 758, routeCandidateFiles 277) so that a broken walk/extension-filter/regex trips them while ordinary deletion — the north star of this gate — does not. If a real deletion wave takes a population under its floor, lower the floor in the same commit and name the wave; do NOT raise a floor to silence anything, and do NOT delete a key (a missing floor FAILS, by design, so an unfloored population cannot exist). A --root fixture run must supply its own --ratchet with fixture-sized minima.

Read by compare-and-swap, not by SELECT. server/jobs/scheduler.ts acquires the single-flight lease with `UPDATE job_locks SET ... WHERE jobName = ? AND (expiresAt < now OR lockedBy = me) RETURNING id` — the WHERE clause IS the read and the RETURNING row is the answer. A separate SELECT-then-UPDATE would reintroduce exactly the race the lock exists to prevent, so this table can never grow a reader the linter's `.from(`/`db.query.` patterns can see. Structural blind spot, not dead weight.

Exported for the injectable-storage seam the module header describes; production consumes the singleton declared four lines below it (`export const investorVerificationService = new InvestorVerificationService()`), so the class has no EXTERNAL production consumer by construction and never can. It was not on this list before unit 53 for a reason worth recording: its only "consumer" was a STALE COMMENT — `// TODO(tsc): InvestorVerificationService exposes no listAllVerifications()` in routes-investor-verification.ts. This linter tokenises identifiers across production files and never distinguishes code from prose, so a comment naming a symbol makes it look reached. (The same mechanism, from the other side, is why scripts/check-org-scoped-fetch.mjs is now in SYMBOL_REGISTERS: its tenancy debt register named a module orphan and resurrected it.) Unit 53 deleted that TODO (it was false: the DB-backing wave HAD added listVerifications(orgId), which is now wired), and the deletion revealed the export. Deletion-revealed, not built-unwired — the same category the table-count notes below already carve out. Verified by re-adding the comment: the gate goes back to PASS at 654 with no code change.

DELIBERATELY-STAGED SEAM, founder ruling (picker, 2026-08-15). The three mounted /developer/* endpoints in routes-epic-services.ts were REMOVED — they were customer-reachable behind plain isAuthenticated, minted `acr_…` keys that NOTHING verified (the only consumer, mcp-server.ts, matches provider='mcp_api_key' while these wrote provider='api_key'), and served a document titled 'AcreOS Public API' — while routes-api-keys.ts is kept dormant to honour the same 'no public API before ~50 customers' ladder. The SERVICE is kept on purpose: what was wrong was mounting the surface early, not writing the OpenAPI spec and the key-minting helper. When the ladder trigger fires this module is the starting point, and wiring it means building the verifier that never existed. Removing its callers is what made it an orphan, so this is deletion-revealed, not built-and-abandoned. expansionLadder.test.ts asserts BOTH directions: no mounted route may mint a key or serve the spec, AND this file must still exist.

EXPANSION-LADDER HOLD — the same standing founder decision that keeps routes-api-keys.ts and developerApiService.ts dormant: 'no public API before ~50 customers' (CLAUDE.md DO-NOT-DO list, expansion ladder). This file IS the public API's mount point: it exports registerPublicApiV1(app), which app.use()s /api/v1/leads, /api/v1/properties and /api/v1/webhooks, and it has ZERO callers anywhere in server/ — its own header documents the two lines to add when the trigger fires, and tests/unit/expansionLadder.test.ts pins BOTH directions (the export must still exist, and server/routes.ts must NOT contain 'registerPublicApiV1('). Not built-and-abandoned: deliberately staged and test-guarded. Only the MOUNT POINT is exempted, deliberately — its three sub-routers stay COUNTED in the unregisteredRoutes baseline so the dormant surface cannot quietly grow. Adding server/api-v1/<anything>.ts fails this gate, which is precisely the bypass a directory-wide exemption would have reopened. When the ladder trigger fires and this is mounted, it stops being a candidate, THIS ENTRY GOES STALE AND THE GATE FAILS until someone removes it and drops the baseline to 1 — mounting the public API cannot be a quiet edit.

TEST-INTROSPECTION SEAM, and the seam is the point. This IS the production Box 1 / Box 4 rule — deriveForm1098, one screen below in this same file, calls it on every 1098 the batch generator emits — so it is reached in every sense except the one this linter can see (it wants a consumer in a DIFFERENT production file). It is exported so refundReversesLedgerAnd1098.test.ts can drive the REAL splitter over the REAL ledger rows a refund webhook wrote, rather than restating the IRS rule in the test. Dropping the export would force the gate to either re-implement 'which box does a reversal land in' (the exact drift CLAUDE.md's canonical-function law warns about: a rule the test checks that is not the rule the product computes) or to reach it only through deriveForm1098's $600 threshold, which cannot express a sub-threshold Box 4 case at all. The value has a production consumer; what has no external consumer is the keyword.

TEST-INTROSPECTION SEAM. This is the DECODER half of the reversal-link convention whose ENCODER (refundReversalTransactionId, same file) webhookHandlers imports to write the ledger row; toOriginatedLedgerEntries calls it on every payments row the 1098 collector reads, so it is live production code. It is exported so the gate can assert the round trip against BOTH producers — the card encoder here and achAutopay's reversalTransactionId — rather than against a hardcoded string. A test pinned to the literal ':return' or '::refund::' is precisely the gate that stays green while the writer renames its format and this parser silently goes blind, reporting refunded interest to the IRS as received.

TEST-INTROSPECTION SEAM. collectOriginatedCandidates (same file) calls this on every `payments` row behind every originated 1098 — it is the production mapping, not a helper for tests. Exported so refundReversesLedgerAnd1098.test.ts can run the rows the refund handler ACTUALLY wrote into the fake database through the REAL mapping and assert on the tax figure that comes out. The alternative is a test that re-implements the two rules living here (post only `completed` rows; drop a reversal whose original was itself struck, or an ACH return subtracts the same interest twice) — a copy that would keep passing while the real mapping changed.

TEST-INTROSPECTION SEAM, same shape and same reason as its originated twin above: collectAcquiredCandidates (same file) calls it on every `note_payments` row behind every acquired 1098. Exported so the gate drives the REAL acquired mapping — specifically that an NSF reversal carries the ORIGINAL payment's date across, which is what decides whether it nets out of Box 1 or invalidates an already-filed prior-year form. A test that built Form1098LedgerEntry values by hand would assert nothing about that carry.

TEST-ONLY CANONICAL REGISTRY — a deliberate shape, recorded here 2026-08-21 because widening the lens to `shared` is the first time anything forced the question. This file is an INDEX OF ENFORCEMENT, not enforcement. Every entry points at where its rule actually lives (a code invariant, a ratchet test, a lint), and a drift-prevention test checks that every pointer still resolves. That satisfies two of the three legs the second CLAUDE.md law demands — authoritative semantics and drift prevention — and deliberately forgoes the third, production adoption, because there is nothing at runtime to adopt: the product does not need to READ the index in order to obey the rules it indexes. THE LAW'S ACTUAL DANGER IS NOT 'NO CALLERS'. It is production computing the same rule INDEPENDENTLY, which is what made publicMaturityOf() a defect — the landing re-implemented its one-line body inline, so the function and the product could disagree. Searched 2026-08-21: nothing in server/ or client/src enumerates these entries on its own, and the only production mention of CANONICAL_OBJECTS anywhere is a comment in enrichmentToClaims.ts pointing AT canon rather than restating it. An index and its targets is the right relationship and the opposite of duplication. WHAT WOULD REVOKE THIS: if a production surface ever computes one of these rules independently instead of consuming the registry, this exemption is wrong and the fix is to make that surface consume the projection — not to widen the exemption. canon.ts: 7 layers, 15 laws, 18 canonical objects, 12 fitness functions; consumed by canonicalArchitecture.test.ts and opportunity.test.ts.

DELETION-REVEALED, same category and same shape as InvestorVerificationService above. The class is exported for the injectable-storage seam; production consumes the SINGLETON declared below it (`export const creditBenchmarkingService = new CreditBenchmarkingService()` at creditBenchmarking.ts:359, class at :87), which server/services/landCredit.ts:1205 dynamically imports and calls. So the class has no EXTERNAL production consumer by construction and never can. Its last apparent consumer was GET /api/land-credit/benchmark/:propertyId in routes-platform-features.ts, which did `const { CreditBenchmarkingService } = await import(...)` and `new CreditBenchmarkingService()` — and that handler was DELETED on 2026-08-27 because it was (a) unreachable behind routes-land-credit.ts:100 and (b) carried a cross-tenant IDOR: neither of its two reads named an organization, and land_credit_scores has no organizationId column, so the org-owned properties row IS the tenancy boundary and it queried by bare id. Deleting a dead handler that would have leaked across tenants is not a regression in reachability, and raising the internal-only baseline to absorb it would have recorded the opposite. The SERVICE stays reachable and is the right place to port a real, org-gated benchmark lookup into the live handler, which today reads score/type/state from the query string and benchmarks zeroes on every call.

lastBumpNote:
2026-08-20 — THE IDENTIFIER PASS STOPPED READING COMMENTS, AND FAMILY 1 SPLIT IN TWO. Four baselines moved and NOT ONE of the moves is a change in how much dead code the repo holds; read them as the gate becoming able to say what was always true. (a) unreachedExports 1395 -> 390. NOT a deletion. 1,005 of those findings were exports used inside their own module and nowhere else, which is a different defect with a different remedy, and they moved to the new internalOnlyExports family (1188, seeded here). Anyone reading 1395 -> 390 as a cleanup is reading it wrong; nothing was deleted in this commit. The split exists because merged, the 390 real accusations sat under 1,188 harmless over-exports at four to one, and a gate whose findings are mostly noise teaches its readers to skim it. (b) opaqueExports 120 -> 23. A REAL narrowing of the blind spot, not a reclassification of dead code: 97 of the 120 were exports the dynamically-imported module itself used, which opacity was never protecting — opacity exempts from the DEATH accusation, and 'stop exporting this' is not that. The family that accuses still keeps the exemption absolutely. (c) moduleOrphans 28 -> 30, and this is the one RAISE. Both files were always orphans; the gate could not see them because their only export was certified reached by a sentence. server/services/agentOrchestration.ts (1,317 lines, zero importers, zero tests) and server/services/lateFees/index.ts (the 12 C.F.R. 1026.36(c)(2) non-pyramiding assessor named in this file's own description as the original worked example of built-but-unwired). NEITHER is absorbed silently and neither is allowlisted, because neither is a deliberately-staged seam: both are recorded on the frontier for adjudication, and they are separate decisions of different kinds. agentOrchestration owns agent_sessions and agent_session_steps exclusively, so deleting it makes two tables writerless AND readerless and the honest version of that deletion includes a DROP migration on tables whose contents nobody has checked — founder territory. lateFees is a REGULATED OBLIGATION built and never wired; its remedy is WIRING, and the live path (jobs/acquiredNoteAging.ts) is advisory BY DESIGN — its header says it 'touches no ledger, and moves nothing' — so turning an advisory into a ledger-writing assessment is a product ruling, not a gate fix. Raising a baseline to absorb a truth correction is defensible exactly once per correction and only when the correction is written down; this is that note. WHAT MADE THE STRIP SAFE. Ledger 35 stripped the two EXEMPTION-granting import scans and deliberately stopped short of the identifier pass, because that one ACCUSES: a wrong exemption hides a finding, a wrong accusation names innocent code. It landed only after the whole revealed population was read rather than counted — all 86 newly-revealed symbols searched by hand across server/, client/src/, shared/ and scripts/ — and ZERO of them had an external reference the pass would now miss. Of the 20 genuine accusations it produced, NINE have real behavioural tests exercising them and no production caller at all, which is the disguise this whole gate exists to see through.

PRIOR (2026-08-19, unreachedExports 1398 -> 1395): unreachedExports 1398 -> 1395 on 2026-08-19: THE GATE WAS READING COMMENTS. lint-reachability scans raw source with regexes, and its two import scanners had no idea what a comment is — so a specifier inside prose granted this gate's two strongest exemptions: a dynamic-import specifier in a comment marked the whole target module `opaque` (every export in it unassertable), and a `from "./x"` in a comment recorded x as imported, so isModuleOrphan(x) returned false. Found the accidental way: a comment written in scripts/check-model-ids.mjs to explain that a vestigial dynamic import had been REMOVED kept the removal from taking effect — the counters did not move until the sentence describing the deleted line was itself reworded. stripCommentsPreservingLines() now feeds both scans (line structure preserved, so reported line numbers still point where they did), with a 10-case self-test printed on every run because a stripper that returned "" would empty every scan and turn this gate green. That revealed three service modules NOTHING loads, each of which had been reading as imported because its own docblock opened with a usage example — `import { commDedup } from "./communicationDeduplication";` — which the scanner read as the module importing itself: atlasContextInjector.ts (344 L), communicationDeduplication.ts (132 L), userAiCostControls.ts (234 L). The gate that exists to find built-and-unwired code was certifying it wired on the strength of the sentence explaining how one day it might be. All three deleted, and none was a close call: the 2026-08 audit had already reviewed two of them (09-correctness.md:68 'zero callers (dead code, TOCTOU moot)'; 16-cost.md F-16-3 'either wire it or delete it and correct the registry'), and each duplicated a live canonical owner with a WEAKER mechanism — commDedup is a Redis-or-in-memory-Map check-then-act against the DB-backed outward-action ledger + idempotencyKey that emailService and directMailService already use; userAiCostControls is a spend cap whose usage read catches everything and falls back to a per-process Map, i.e. it fails OPEN and silently disables itself, beside the DB-backed intelligence/budget, founderInboxBudget, credits and outreachStopLoss; atlasContextInjector eagerly assembled portfolio state into every Pax turn that Pax already fetches on demand via get_deals / get_stale_leads / get_tasks / get_pipeline_summary. Net -2 not -3, because deleting the injector revealed its own dependency: buildPaxSystemPromptAddition in paxRelationshipArc.ts had exactly one production consumer and it was the dead injector. That one was deleted too (-1 more, hence 1395) rather than left counted, and it is worth why: the block it rendered said "You MAY take autonomous actions ... without explicit permission", granted on a stage that advances on an interaction COUNTER. It had never appeared in a prompt. Wiring it would put a permission grant in a channel with no authority to issue one — autonomy here is decided by autonomyGuardrails/autonomousAgentEngine.evaluate and enforced in executeTool's approval kernel — so it would not widen authority, only make Pax attempt refused actions and make the next reader believe usage buys it. getRelationshipState/getStageBehavior/recordPaxInteraction stay: they are live behind /api/pax/relationship. STILL OPEN, measured the same day and deliberately not taken here: the IDENTIFIER pass still reads raw source, so a comment merely NAMING a symbol still counts as a production use of it — stripping there too moves unreachedExports 1398 -> 1478, i.e. 80 exports are currently certified reached by a sentence. That is an 80-item adjudication and this ratchet is down-only, so it cannot land in halves; it is on the frontier. PRIOR NOTE — unreachedExports 1399 -> 1398 on 2026-08-18: `analyzeHighestBestUse` and its four supporting types/helpers were DELETED with `EnvironmentalIntelligenceCard` and `POST /api/environmental/highest-best-use` (founder ruling, picker). Net -1 rather than -5 because the same commit's GBM work added `assumedFeatures` to a return shape that is consumed immediately, and the valuation methodology string reads it. Worth recording WHY the HBU code was not preserved for a rebuild: it carried the defect class this wave is chasing — per-use scores started at a hardcoded base and were adjusted by string-matching free-text zoning/utilities/road fields, then returned as an `estimatedValueImpact`. The card that was its only caller had zero importers AND issued the query as a GET against a POST route, so the analysis had never run for anyone. Deletion remains the cheapest way to satisfy this gate. Locked in per the strictly-down rule. PRIOR NOTE — unreachedExports 1400 -> 1399 on 2026-08-18: FOUNDRY TRANSFER — OUTCOME OBSERVATION, second layer. `outcomeBasis()` in server/services/autopilot/experienceLog.ts gained its FIRST production caller. Worth recording because of what it was: its docstring drew exactly the distinction the autopilot's learning loop most needed — 'lets callers refine the causal model from real CONSEQUENCE only, never the execution proxy' — and only a test had ever called it, while `outcomeOf`, which everything calls, voted a clean dispatch as a full-weight success. The repository had written the rule down in a function nothing consulted and broken it in the function everything consulted. That is CLAUDE.md's second law (a canonical function with zero production callers is not canonical), third recorded instance after publicMaturityOf and isFounderUserId. The fix did not delete the function to satisfy this gate — it made the founder's story surface consume it, so the basis of every verdict now ships to the person reading it. Locked in per the strictly-down rule. PRIOR NOTE — 2026-08-18, FOUNDRY TRANSFER — PUSH DISPATCH SEMANTICS — unreachedExports 1401 -> 1400. NOT a deletion: an existing governance primitive got its FIRST production consumer. server/services/founder.ts exports isFounderUserId(), the canonical 'is this Clerk id a founder' check, and it had ZERO production callers — an authority helper that existed, was exported, and enforced nothing anywhere. sendPushToPerson() now calls it to authorize the recipient of a person-global push, so the helper is reached and the notification channel stops taking its recipient on trust. Net -1 even though the same change ADDED two exports (PushDispatchStatus, PushResult), both of which have real consumers — the nudger and the background runner both branch on the status, and the type is destructured by four existing callers. Locked in per the strictly-down rule, in the commit that earned it. PRIOR NOTE — 2026-08-16, BYO SEND-RAIL REMEDIATION — unreachedExports 1402 -> 1401 and tablesNoReader 61 -> 60, both attributed by measuring HEAD against the working tree and diffing symbol by symbol. (A) tablesNoReader: borrower_payment_profiles now has a READER. It is a CLASS B table (customer records) that the 2026-08-16 triage deliberately did not drop, and the new reader is the founder-ruled autopilot guard — counterpartyMatch() queries it, along with leads / borrower_sessions / autopay_enrollments / buyer_reservations, to refuse any autopilot send addressed to a customer's counterparty. A dead table became live because a rule started being enforced, which is the direction this gate wants. (B) unreachedExports: the wave first ADDED three exports and the gate correctly failed on growth — counterpartyMatch, ORG_IDENTITY_BLOCK_REASON and isOrgIdentityRefusal, every one exported purely so its test could import it while its only production caller sat one line away in the same module.
